bounded_question: How does node #115 Find a component by name: the Find entry point 0x609e510, the normalizer 0x609a410, the '=' options parser 0x60c1190, the options-map merge, and the delegate table search (worker 0x6097630, matcher 0x60bb9a0, resolver 0x60971c0) -- and what does each step pin down about that path?

census.method: one objdump pass over work/hl-node-115.bin; direct call/jmp targets and lea comment addresses matched against the packet's routines; enclosing FDE per site (see census.py)

cstr_ctor.behaviour: std::string construct from a C string: strlen, SSO (<= 15) or _M_create + memcpy; throws __throw_logic_error (string at 0x963298, 'basic_string: construction from null is not valid') when the C string is null

cstr_replace.behaviour: _M_replace(dst, 0, len, cstr, strlen(cstr)): assign a C string to an existing std::string

delegate_impl.behaviour: calls the object's vtable slot 0x48 (rdi = out, rsi = obj); reached from fallback_delegate 0x6097150 (r8d = 0) and from 0x6099e70.. at 0x609a032

fallback.behaviour: out zeroed at entry; b non-null -> delegate to fallback_delegate 0x6097150 (out-temp rsp+0x20, b) and move the temp out into the real out; b null and c+0x18 == 0 -> out stays zeroed (success); b null and c+0x18 != 0 -> Status code 4, msg1 = '', msg2 = 'Cannot configure null object ' (29 chars, trailing space), rendered ': Cannot configure null object '

find_entry.behaviour: out zeroed at entry. (a) name empty or equal to the global default (0x6508980) -> clear the r8 string via _M_replace(0, len, '', 0), call map-clear 0x5d5b300(map), return. (b) delegate null -> call find_norm 0x609ea72 with an empty-string fallback and return. (c) delegate non-null -> call delegate vtable slot 0x78 (returns a std::string by sret into rsp+0xd0), then find_norm(out-temp rsp+0x70, name, fallback = delegate-string, outstr = r8, ctx = map); the temp out is MOVED into the real out (0x609e5c4); if out byte0 != 0 -> return. (d) if out byte0 == 0 -> delegate-name check: slot 0x80's target vs canonical GOT 0x64eceb8 (0x5d2e770); if different, call slot 0x80(delegate, r8-string) as a predicate (false -> return); if equal, compare the r8-string against slot 0x70's string, else slot 0x90's string (strlen + memcmp); a mismatch returns directly. (e) register path on a match: deep-copy the 0x50-byte value struct into a temp at rsp+0xd0 (taking shared ownership of the +0x48 control), replace the temp's name string wholesale with ';' via _M_replace(0, len, 0x43d5c7, 1), call thunk 0x6098510 -> worker 0x6097630; if the worker out byte0 != 0 -> cleanup + return (the worker error is swallowed); if 0 -> parse the worker's accumulated string (NOT the empty string) with the parser into a fresh temp map at rsp+0x70 (header {buckets-ptr = rsp+0xa0, bucket_count = 1, first = 0, count = 0, max_load = 1.0f, next_resize = 0, single_bucket = 0}) and merge the temp map's entries into the real map insert-if-absent (existing keys are NOT overwritten; the merge loop at 0x609e8b8 walks the temp list, linear-walks (<= 20) or bucket-walks the real map, skips found keys). A parser failure on this path is also swallowed: its message is freed, the temp map is destroyed (0x5d36110), and find_entry returns the success status left by find_norm

census.note: includes host 0x60779af (see #3386: 21 call sites incl. the host)

find_entry.signature: find_entry(out, value-struct, delegate, name-string, name-out-string, map)

find_norm.behaviour: out zeroed; name empty or equal to the global default -> assign the fallback to the out-string, return; else find '=' (0x3d) in the name: not found -> assign the name to the out-string, return; found -> call the parser (temp-out rsp+0x10, name, ctx): move the parser out into out; if out byte0 != 0 -> assign the name to the out-string, call map-clear 0x5d5b300(ctx), clear out (zero the whole status back to success) and return -- the parser error is swallowed; if out byte0 == 0 -> 'id' path: look up key 'id' (built as an SSO string, len 2, chars 0x6469) in the map via 0x609a1b0; if found -> out-string = the node's value string, call map-erase 0x609a2f0(map, node), and if the out-string then equals the global default name -> clear it (len 0, first byte 0); if not found -> if the fallback len == 0 -> assign the name, call map-clear; else assign the fallback. Return

literals.value: Mismatched curly braces for nested options

map_clear.behaviour: walk the node list at map+0x10, destroy both strings per node, sized-delete each 0x50-byte node, memset the buckets array to zero, zero +0x10 and +0x18

map_erase.behaviour: bucket from the node hash (+0x48) % bucket_count, walk the chain to unlink (fixing the bucket pointer and map+0x10 first-node if needed), destroy both strings, sized-delete the 0x50-byte node, decrement the element count; returns the node's next pointer

map_find.behaviour: linear walk (<= 20 elements) comparing key len (+0x10) + memcmp; else _Hash_bytes + bucket walk comparing the stored hash (+0x48), key len, memcmp. Buckets point to the node BEFORE the bucket's first node (libstdc++ before-begin trick). Returns node* or null

map_index.behaviour: operator[]: find by hash/key; if absent, allocate a 0x50-byte node, copy the key via 0x60b7cd0 (range assign), value starts as '' (ptr = &buf+0x38, len 0), store the hash at +0x48, link into the bucket (rehash via 0x5d38260 when _M_need_rehash says so, called at 0x60c0fe2), element count++. Insert position: after the bucket's before-begin node; empty bucket -> list head (the old first node's bucket pointer moves to the new node; the new node's own bucket pointer becomes the map+0x10 sentinel). Returns &node->value string (node+0x28)

matcher.behaviour: rsi is node+0x28 (the object pointer), so offsets are node+0x28+off: if the prefix (r8) is 0 -> out zeroed (no match); if node+0xd4 == 4 -> no match; if node+0xd8 & 0x2000 -> Status code 3, msg1 = the name, msg2 = 'Cannot serialize option: ' (25 chars, trailing space); if node+0x60 != 0 -> virtual call *0x40(node+0x28) (rdi = out, rsi = node+0x50, rdx = value, rcx = name, r8 = &temp-string holding prefix + movslq(node+0x28), r9 = &temp) which fills out directly. Kind dispatch on node+0xd0: 0x16 -> 0x60bbbf0 path; 0x15 -> resolver path (0x60bba43); any other kind -> serializer path (0x60bbb78). 0x15 path: flag checks on node+0xd8 & 0x800/0x400/0x200 -> if any set, walk the name-object link rbp = *(rbp) (0x60bbcb0) ONCE and run the body on the linked object; a null link -> out zeroed (no match). Otherwise copy the value struct via 0x60b9d70, replace the copied name with ';' (0x43d5c7), call resolver 0x60971c0(out-temp, name-object at prefix + movslq(node+0x28), value-copy, '' via 0x60b7d80), move the result into the value-out via 0x60b79e0, destroy the copy via 0x5e33fb0, return zeroed. 0x16 path (0x60bbbf0): the value-out is cleared first (0x60bbc70); the same one-link flag-chain walk, but a null link ends in the chain-exhausted handling: if the 0xb1 flag (node+0xd9) is set -> value-out = the global default name (0x6508980 via _M_assign); else if value+0x04 != 0 -> value-out cleared ('' via 0x60b79b0); else -> the default name. If no flags are set: if node+0xd8 & 0x8000 is set AND value+0x28 != 2 -> delegate-name path, gated on value+0x04 == 0 or node+0xd8 & 0x100: call the name object's vtable slot 0x78 (rdi = temp string, rsi = name object), copy the result into the value-out via 0x60b79e0, return zeroed; the same gate with value+0x04 set and 0x100 clear is no match (out zeroed, value-out stays cleared). If 0x8000 is clear or value+0x28 == 2 -> the resolver path (0x60bbcc8): copy the value, replace name with ';', if the 0xb1 flag is set clear the copy's +0x04 byte, call the resolver, then if copy+0x04 == 0 -> assign the result to the value-out; else the result must contain '=' (0x445245, find) -- found -> assign, not found -> clear the value-out via 0x60b79b0. The resolver's result never contains '=' (it is the whole name when the name has no '=', or '{' + the part before the first '=' + '}'), so with +0x04 set and the 0xb1 flag clear the 0x16 resolver path always clears. Serializer path (0x60bbb78): if value+0x04 == 0 -> call the serializer; else if node+0xd8 & 0x100 == 0 -> out zeroed (no match); else call serializer 0x60ba600(object = r8 + movslq(node+0x28 int32), kind = node+0xd0 in esi, out-string = r12 value-out): returns true -> no match (out zeroed); returns false -> Status code 4, msg1 = the name, msg2 = 'Cannot serialize option: '
matcher.signature: matcher(out, node+0x28, value, name, prefix, value-out)

open_unknowns: The sibling entry point 0x609a740..0x609b6f3 (4019 B; the third find_norm caller at 0x609b190; takes 9+ args, copies the 0x50-byte value struct, uses magic 0x692e and a '.' char, calls 0x61d1390) -- a separate entry point with different behavior, a future candidate

The global default name at 0x6508980 (a std::string; compared by length then memcmp in find_entry and find_norm): its runtime value is set by static init, and the initializer was not located. 11 lea reference sites, all readers: 0x6077907 (host), 0x607e8e0, 0x6086c84, 0x609a45e (find_norm), 0x609e567 (find_entry), 0x60a7534, 0x60bbc99 (matcher), 0x60bf710, 0x60bf730, 0x61372c8, 0x61d2974 (an exception/landing-pad path, not an initializer). A 'default' literal sits at 0x44371c in .rodata, but no lea referencing it as this global's initializer was established. The model parameterizes DEFAULT_NAME, defaulting to 'default' as the documented assumption

The delegate vtable base address: the delegate's vtable slots 0x70/0x78/0x80/0x90 and the node+0x28 vtable slots 0x40/0x78 need a base, which was not pinned from locally retained evidence. Only the GOT/canonical entries are pinned (GOT 0x64eceb8 -> 0x5d2e770, 0x64ecf50 -> 0x5d48960, 0x64ecf80 -> 0x5d4d490); see vtables.tsv
The serializer 0x60ba600's per-kind serialization rules (25 jump-table cases, 0..0x18): a documented boundary of this item, not modeled internally
The value struct's +0x48 shared_ptr control vtable base for this item's value objects (the Statistics control vptr 0x64d2f00 was pinned in #3440 for Statistics objects only)
Which construction paths install a non-null +0x28 delegate (the value struct's delegate slot) -- the enable-byte setter and the bucket_count writer at record+0x390 remain open from earlier items

options_map.header: buckets +0x00, bucket_count +0x08, first node +0x10, element_count +0x18, rehash policy +0x20..0x30
options_map.node: next +0x00, std::string key +0x08, std::string value +0x28, u64 hash +0x48; 0x50 bytes
options_map.rehash: 0x5d38260; grow to the smallest libstdc++ prime >= element count + 1; the list is re-linked so same-bucket nodes stay contiguous
options_map.type: libstdc++ unordered_map<std::string, std::string> with before-begin bucket pointers (buckets hold the node before the bucket's first node)

parser.behaviour: trim the name via 0x61d11f0; if len > 2 and it starts with '{' (0x7b) and ends with '}' (0x7d), repeatedly strip outer braces and re-trim; then loop over key=value pairs separated by ';': find_first_of with the delimiter set at 0x44b52b = '={};' (4 chars); the first delimiter must be '=' or error Status code 4 msg2 'Unexpected char in key' (0x44ff0e, 22 chars); the key is trimmed, an empty key -> error code 4 'Empty key found' (0x4362e1, 15 chars); the value is extracted by 0x60b97f0 (separator ';', supports {...} brace groups with depth counting); if value extraction errors -> copy that Status into out via 0x60b7ac0; else store the pair into the ctx map via 0x60c0e90 (operator[] -- insert-if-absent, value default '', then _M_assign(map-value, extracted-value) -- so a duplicate key in one parse is OVERWRITTEN); advance the cursor past ';'; at end (cursor == -1 or cursor >= len) -> out zeroed (success, byte0 == 0). No delimiter found at all -> error code 4 msg2 "Mismatched key value pair, '=' expected" (0x969140, 39 chars). The throw path uses the format string at 0x43e542 ('basic_string::substr...' / 'Unable to persist options.')

rehash.behaviour: libstdc++ unordered_map rehash: grow to the smallest prime >= element count + 1 and re-derive every bucket's before-begin node; the list is re-linked so same-bucket nodes stay contiguous

resolver.behaviour: calls the name-object's vtable slot 0x60 (returns a string by sret into rsp+0x00); if the string has no '=' (0x3d) -> move the whole string into out; else build a new string = '{' + name-up-to-'=' + '}' (literals: 0x44ecd8 is '{' (1 char, bytes 7b 00), 0x432097 is '}' (1 char, bytes 7d 00)), move it into out. The rdx/rcx/r8 args are unused. Self-contained (only PLT callees)

serializer.behaviour: BOUNDARY (not modeled internally): a type-directed value serializer with a jump table at 0x978650 (25 cases, kind 0..0x18); uses basic_string::_M_construct (PLT 0x63f1000, called 14x), numeric formatting with magnitude buckets (9 / 0x63 / 0x3e7 / 0x270f / 0xf423f / 0x98967f / 0x5f5e0ff, magic 0x346dc5d63886594b), and sub-callees 0x5f06bb0, 0x60ba450, 0x61d0f30, 0x61c7e30, 0x60b79e0. Interface contract: true = serialized-OK/continue (matcher: no match), false = Status code 4 in the matcher. Its per-kind rules are an open unknown for a future item

shared_release.note: the shared_ptr control release used by the value struct's +0x48 control (via 0x5d350c0 when non-null) and by the copy path (refcount inc via the 0x64ed290 __libc_single_threaded check)
shared_release.protocol: 0x100000001 fast path calls control slots 0x10/0x18 directly; otherwise atomic-dec, single-threaded flag at 0x64ed290 selects lock-xadd vs plain dec

census.note: the builder is the shared Status constructor used across the node

status_builder.layout: code u8 +0x00, subcode u8 +0x01, severity u8 +0x02, u16 zero +0x03, u8 zero +0x05, msg char* +0x08
status_builder.message_rule: msg1, or msg1 + ': ' + msg2 when msg2 is non-empty; frees the old message with delete[]

status_copy.behaviour: Status move-assign (6 bytes + string, zeroes src, frees dst's old heap string)

thunk.behaviour: signature (out = rdi, delegate = rsi, value = rdx, empty-string = rcx): clears the empty string (len 0, buf[0] = 0), builds a fresh empty temp string, calls worker 0x6097630(out, value, delegate, &fresh-empty-string, &cleared-empty-string). So the worker's 4th arg is the prefix string (empty from the thunk) and its 5th arg is the out-string accumulator

trim.behaviour: copies the string with leading/trailing isspace() removed; empty/all-whitespace -> out = ''

value_copy.behaviour: deep-copies the 0x50-byte value struct (string via 0x60b7cd0, u32 +0x28, u8 +0x2c, 16B +0x38, u64 +0x30, u64 +0x48 with refcount inc on the control)

value_dtor.behaviour: releases the +0x48 control via 0x5d350c0 when non-null, frees the name string's heap buffer (sized delete via _ZdlPvm when the buffer is not the SSO inline buffer)

value_extract.behaviour: skips leading whitespace; if the next char is '{', brace-matching scan (depth +1 on '{', -1 on '}'); unbalanced -> Status code 4 msg2 'Mismatched curly braces for nested options' (0x95ddc0, 42 chars); balanced -> value = trimmed inner content, then skip whitespace and require ';' else error code 4 'Unexpected chars after nested options' (0x964410, 37 chars) -- but if the cursor is at/past end of string after the group, *cursor is left at that position and the parse succeeds (the parser ends on cursor >= len); else find ';' from start -> value = trimmed str[start..p) (or to end if no ';', with *cursor = -1); start >= len -> value-out cleared, *cursor = -1; success -> out zeroed. Calls 0x60b79e0 (value assign) on the trimmed value

value_struct.layout: {u32 +0x00, u8 +0x04, std::string +0x08 (ptr/len/buf16), u32 +0x28, u8 +0x2c, u64 +0x30, 16 bytes +0x38, u64 +0x48} where +0x48 is a shared_ptr control block (use-count at +0x08, released via 0x5d35070 or vtable slots 0x10/0x18 when count is 0x100000001)

vtables.note: the delegate vtable base and the node+0x28 vtable base were not pinned from locally retained evidence; only the GOT/canonical entries below are pinned (see vtables.tsv). The __libc_single_threaded GLOB_DAT at 0x64ed290 is consulted by the shared-control release paths -- not a threads flag

worker.behaviour: iterates the delegate's vector at +0x08..+0x10 of 0x30-byte elements (begin at 0x8(%rsp), end at 0x70(%rsp), +0x30 per element); per element, walks a linked list starting at *(element+0x28)+0x10 (next at +0x00); per node filters: skip if +0xd4 in {4,5} ((x-4) <= 1), skip if +0xd8 & 0x2000; if value+0x04 != 0, extra dispatch (+0xd8 & 0x100 -> copy path 0x6097bd8; +0xd0 in {0x15,0x16} -> path 0x6097ef8); otherwise the common path. Each attempt builds name = prefix-string + node name (the first append is the prefix string, which is empty from the thunk; the element's name-string pointer at element+0x20 is passed to the matcher as its r8 prefix, NOT concatenated into the name) and calls matcher 0x60bb9a0(out-temp rsp+0x80, node+0x28, value, combined-name, prefix = element+0x20, value-out rsp+0x90). There are exactly 3 matcher call sites in the worker: 0x6097853 (common first), 0x6097d82 (copy path), 0x6097fe3 (0x6097ef8 path) -- there is NO second matcher attempt per node. If the matcher out byte0 != 0 -> copy its 6-byte status + string into the real out and RETURN (first match wins). If byte0 == 0 and the value-out string (rsp+0x90; its length is at rsp+0x98) is non-empty -> append name2 = prefix + node name + '=' (0x445245) + value-out into the out-string accumulator (the worker adds NO ';' separator between pairs -- no 0x43d5c7 reference exists in the worker) and continue to the next node; the value-out string is moved into the name build, leaving it empty. If nothing matches -> out zeroed. Length guard constant 0x3fffffffffffffff used in reserve checks. The copy path (0x6097bd8) builds a full 0x50-byte value-struct copy at rsp+0x110 with +0x04 forced to 1 (refcount inc via 0x64ed290 __libc_single_threaded check) and calls the matcher at 0x6097d82 with the copy. The 0x6097ef8 path: if value+0x28 == 2 -> proceed; else if node+0xd8 & 0x8000 -> skip the node entirely (jump 0x60976fb); else build the name and call the matcher at 0x6097fe3 with the original value
